scenes.text: You glance at your phone, and it unlocks in a fraction of a second, even in a dark room, even with new glasses. [1] But a photo of you won't fool it. [2] Let's break down how face unlock works.

Here's what happens in that fraction of a second. [1] The camera captures your face, often with infrared light, so it works in the dark. [2] A detection model finds your face in the frame. [3] A recognition model turns it into a face embedding, a list of numbers unique to you. [4] It compares that with the embedding saved when you set it up, [5] and if they're close enough, it unlocks.

data.heading: In a fraction of a second

scenes.text: Remember embeddings from episode six? Faces work the same way. [1] Every face becomes a point on a map, and different people sit far apart. [2] Your face today, with new glasses, lands on the map, [3] and it's closest to your own saved face, so it unlocks.

But what stops someone from holding up your photo? [1] That's called liveness detection. [2] Depth sensing checks that your face is 3D, not a flat photo. [3] It looks for natural signs, like tiny movements. [4] And some phones check that your eyes are open, and looking at the screen.

data.definition: Checking that a real, live face is in front of the camera, not a photo or a mask.

scenes.text: Here are four terms. [1] Enrolment, when you first set up face unlock, and it saves your face embedding. [2] The threshold, how close a match must be to unlock. [3] A false accept, letting the wrong person in. [4] And a false reject, not recognising you.

And not all face unlock is equal. [1] Basic 2D face unlock uses only the normal camera, so a good photo can sometimes fool it. [2] 3D face unlock uses depth sensors, so it's much harder to fool, and secure enough for payments.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think their face photo is uploaded to the cloud for face unlock. [2] On most phones, the face data stays on the device, in a secure chip, and never leaves it. Still, it's worth checking your phone's settings.

data.myth: My face photo is uploaded to the cloud for face unlock.
data.fact: On most phones, face data stays on the device in a secure chip.
